COVID: Ground zero

By: Tarryn Crossman | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Its been over a month since news broke of South Africa's first case of COVID 19, as the numbers increase how are we getting ready for what is coming

Summary:
I will add all the people tomorrow, just waiting to hear from Private and state

Further information:
On the 5th of March South Africa confirmed its first case of COVID 19, the dreaded corona virus was on our shores. We look at how the ministry of health reacted, what plans were put in place and where are we today.
How is our overcrowded, under resourced health system going to cope with the influx of patients?

How does this affect other state patients: clinics and other facilities refusing to treat people as they don’t have the gear, a lack of medication

Gift of the givers were preparing to deliver relief once the storm hit, but they soon realised in South Africa even in the eye of storm relief was needed. They immediately started getting requests for masks, gloves and sanitiser, as health workers across South Africa scrambled to keep themselves safe in the field. They started putting up tents to screen patients before they entered hospitals in an attempt to prevent COVID 19 patients from contaminating others. They setup tents in KZN, CT and JHB. They are distributing 100 000’s of respiratory protective gear across the country

Private facilities are also creating pre-screening areas to keep COVID patients separate. They are increasing their ICU bed space and heading to a point where all visits will be suspended except for in the maternity ward.

The NICD have studied what has happened in other countries, they will give us the facts and stats. Where are we heading, are we ready and what do we need to do to get there. If we don’t get there what happens

Transcript
Coid 19 Ground Zero
10 minutes 04 seconds

Characters

DR KARIM
DR SOOLIMAN
MEC BANDILE MASUKU
MACFARLAN

1 00:00 VO Mac: For the first time in human history the world is fighting one common enemy. A virus that is spreading like wildfire from country to country. Globally there are now over 2 million people infected with COVID 19. But How did a virus that started in a city in China take over the world
2 00:16 DR Karim The whole world has never encountered this virus there is no protection, no vaccine, no antibodies. This virus is spreading, that’s what it does it does nothing else
3 00:27 V/O Professor Salim Abdool Karim is a world renowned epidemiologist and infectious diseases specialist. He is currently the chairperson of the ministerial advisory group on COVID 19, which was formed after South Africa confirmed its first case On the 5th of March this advisory group are intrinsic in every decision that is made to beat this virus
4 00:48 Dr Karim We only take queries from the minister and acting director general. We put small
teams together to go and investigate, all of that is done in a matter of hours. We are Building the ship while we are sailing. Feels like we are in a fast and furious movie
5 01:16 V/O As our numbers climbed to just over 400 confirmed infections The presidency made the decision to declare an unprecedented national lockdown, which started at midnight on the 26th of March.
6 01:29 Karim We have this reprieve largely due to early proactive approach of our government,
but that’s just a temporary reprieve. It is going to spread; we have not ducked this bullet we have simply slowed it down
7 02:12 VO Under the guidance of the advisory board South African rolled out over 28000 field workers into high density areas increasing testing more than 20 fold in two weeks. But still the numbers weren’t going up. Which is currently been attributed toour initial international travel ban and strict nationwide lockdown
8 02:30 Dr Karim We have this reprieve largely due to early proactive approach of our government,
but that’s just a temporary reprieve. It is going to spread; we have not ducked this bullet we have simply slowed it down
9 02:50 Mac Link The war on Corona has given South Africa a mutual enemy, one that require the state, private business and civil society to work together in order to beat it. Never before has been so imperative for South Africa to come together.
10 03:04 VO If we don’t win this war the President himself has said it will engulf and ultimately consume our country” Gift of the givers is the one of the biggest disaster relief Non-governmental organisation in Africa, They have been at ground zero since day one helping the government prepare for what is
coming Dr Imtiaz Sooliman is the founder of the organisation
11 03:27 DR Sooliman Well when it started off you know in China we already started thinking of it then
And our focus at that point was still at the end game because the end game was when the massage start coming in huge numbers and they need ventilation and they need care. And that’s a time it’s a lifesaving phase. So I said lets wait for that phase and see what happens. But everything changed. message just come in and then suddenly all the medical professionals the hospital superintendent or manager said look first thing again we need M95 we need latex gloves. We need coveralls. We need the head covering the shoe covering. And then the alarm bells went on when a private sector doctor started calling
we realized that the medical professionals were scared and we said now we’re going have a major problem more than the virus. What happens if medical professionals are afraid to see patients?
12 04:07 VO Health workers are on the frontline of the fight against the virus, but due to an overwhelming shortage of personal protective equipment many are being unnecessarily exposed.
The MEC for health in Gauteng Dr Bandile Masuku worked in some of the biggest state hospitals for years before taking office.
13 04:27 MEC BANDILE Withut health workers there is no way of overcoming the pandemic. it is our preoccupation. We’ve created the WhatsApp a group for everyone. Any health worker to have access to a report if this they are running short or they don’t have
14 04:43 VO Across the provinces we have seen an increase in health workers testing positive for COVID 19 In Kwazulu Natal Two netcare hospitals, St Augustines and Kingsway have collectively had almost 60 staff members test positive. Parts of both hospitals have been shutdown. In jhb At Morningside Mediclinic nearly 20 staff members tested positive
15 05:07 DR KARIM we are going to see outbreaks everywhere. Prisons, hospitals if you don’t see it you are not living on planet earth. Because this virus is spreading
16 05:17 VO South Africa has set up a solidarity fund for the private sector to make donations, to date it has raised over 2 billion rand. Some of which will be used to purchase personal protective equipment. Gift of the givers is also expecting a large shipment of PPE’s
16 05:34 Sooliman We are just buying everything off
17 05:37 VO Although there is a massive effort being made to relieve the crises, By the department of healths current estimates our health services are short 72 million pairs of gloves, and 82 million face masks. 10 million N95 masks, and 160,000 face shields.
To stop the virus from spreading through the provinces border patrols have been setup across the country during lockdown. Prohibiting anyone from traveling without the correct permits
18 06:07 Cop There are still vehicles coming through from the other provinces but have clear instructions they need to turn back.
19 06:16 At all these roadblocks travellers are being screened for potential COVID-19 symptoms .

You should just come in and 1 patient has tested positive for Covid 19
20 06:26 VO In an attempt to buy us more time, on the 9th of April South Africa’s lockdown was extended
21 06:32 KARIM If we end the lockdown abruptly we will intermingle our high and low risk and move into a generalised spread it will just get ahead of us. While we are buying time.
22 06:51 Voice over People will get sick, but every action taken on the ground right now will affect how many and our health systems capacity to take care of them.
As Another line of defence against COVID 19 the national department of health has setup triage tents Dr Peter Beskyd is a emergency physician consulting at Chris Hani Baragwaneth hospital
23 07:14 Dr Peter Beskyd Everyone who is going to enter the hospital is going to be triaged, so we can def screen them to make sure we aren’t allowing any suspect patients to enter the clean areas of the hospital and secondly the size of the tents we have used has allowed us to keep patient to patient distances that will negate or minimise the spread from patient to patient
24 07:32 Voice over Statistically the health ministry has estimated that 60% of South Africa will get the virus and of that 60% 20 % will need some form of medical treatment over a 6 month period. That it is a potential 700 000 South Africans that will be trying to get access to already under resourced hospitals.
25 07:53 KARIM We creating field hospitals anyone that is sick goes to field hospital they don’t go to hopistals we have to protect hospitals
26 08: 05 VO National policy states that if you can self-isolate you must, but for those that can’t isolation centres are being setup in all the provinces.
27 08:14 MEC places that were given to us and offered to us by the state owned enterprises. Your Eskom, Transnet and telekom. Which gave us a beds around 1000 beds
28 08:24 Voice over The Johannesburg expo centre formally known as NSREC has also been setup to accommodate 500 patients in isolation with basic medical care. It has the potential to accommodate 2000
Because COVID 19 is a respiratory disease it is estimated that 5% of the worse cases will need to be ventilated
At this point in both private and state there are only about 6000 ventilators available nationally. If this virus gets to the predicted numbers South Africa will have a national short fall of 100 000’s of ventilators
29 09:03 Karim There is no country in the world that has enough intensive care uinits has enough beds or ventilators or doctors. Has enough capability just can’t because were the pandemic grows it grows so fast.
30 09:22 Soolimsn
For the love of money you cant get any ventilators in the world, there's a possibilty we coiuld only get 70 ventilators in the next 4 weeks
31 09:27 VO Governemtn has launched a natyional ventilator project, which is working with the private sector to build 10 000 non invasive ventilators by the end of June
32 09:37 Karim I believe that if we can put out the flames before they become fires I think we will flatten this curve enough that even at peak we will be able to deal with the burden
We want to safe lives and the extend with which we can do that will be a reflection of whether the decisions we made were right or wrong
